capturePolicy: Short paraphrase captures only. Locators point to official pages; no page is treated as proof beyond its stated scope.

captures.capture: Movement is divided into normal direction, walk, sprint, stance changes, jump/vault and lean, giving space traversal a small, learnable verb set.
A world-pointing input becomes both an on-screen and map marker; the stated design goal is quicker, clearer teammate communication.
A changing spatial boundary turns elapsed time into route pressure and imposes a continuous cost for remaining outside the viable area.
Radar, remaining time and current mission state occupy separate readable surfaces; controls, sensitivity and audio are configurable.
Audio attention can be tuned and critical events can receive redundant visual or spatial feedback, although the documented examples are combat-specific.

captures.locator: Stage 2 Prototype through Stage 5 Content Complete
captures.capture: Reality references are filtered through disposable blockouts, then navigation, door, AI, interactable and sightline passes before content completion.

captures.locator: Civilian AI Modifiers and Miscellaneous Modifiers
captures.capture: Civilian response is a variable rather than a guaranteed animation, while door state changes what can be seen and how costly a path is.
The threat reacts to player behavior and avoids becoming fully predictable; this produces uncertainty without requiring an invisible random-failure roll.
Systemic, minimally constrained behavior is paired with authored animation quality, separating behavioral variability from visual incoherence.

captures.locator: built from the ground up for virtual reality
captures.capture: Tasks are represented as manipulating specific world objects and tools, while locomotion and input are offered through more than one method.

captures.locator: official feature list and operations paragraph
captures.capture: A hazardous scene becomes a coordination problem among teammates, tools, changing fire states and rescue goals, with more than one possible solution.
Single-player leadership is expressed through task assignment to AI crew and direct participation, which makes delegation observable rather than menu-only.
